summary: The blueprint broadly covers healthy human pancreas but needs targeted refinement of mixed lymphoid axes and modest stromal/rare-endocrine marker cleanup.

issues.description: The blueprint merges biologically distinct lymphoid populations into two mixed modules: T cells with NK/cytotoxic cells, and B cells with plasma cells. For an all-cell human pancreas embedding, these should be represented as separate immune identities rather than forced onto combined axes.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the broad lymphoid modules and axes with separate immune-gated modules/axes for T cells, NK/cytotoxic cells, B cells, and plasma cells, reusing the current markers split into coherent sets and adding canonical markers such as XBP1 or PRDM1 for plasma cells if supported.

issues.description: The fibroblast_stellate module largely reflects ECM-producing fibroblast or activated stellate signal and does not clearly distinguish pancreatic fibroblasts from stellate or activated-stellate biology.
issues.suggested_fix: Add or revise mesenchymal gated axes to separate fibroblast/ECM identity from stellate or myofibroblast/activated-stellate state, while retaining the existing mural/pericyte resolution.

issues.description: The PP/gamma and epsilon modules include several broadly endocrine or overlapping markers such as IAPP, PCSK1, ISL1, and RBP4, which may reduce subtype specificity against beta, delta, and endocrine-core axes.
issues.suggested_fix: Trim or replace the least specific overlapping genes with more subtype-selective markers from the cited pancreas atlases, while retaining enough markers for robust rare-cell scoring.

out_of_scope: Citation and DOI verification was not reassessed.
The epithelial_ductal_bias axis is somewhat redundant but not biologically wrong.
